"The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook." While the near-term shock is clearly negative, the Committee’s swift move to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repo operations, and discount window easing are consistent with the credit-channel literature showing that accommodative policy can lower the external finance premium and support investment and spending when balance sheets are stressed (Bernanke-Gertler; Gertler and Gilchrist 1994; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994; Oliner and Rudebusch 1996a). With market-based inflation compensation falling and survey expectations little changed, the literature on inflation targeting and central bank credibility (Svensson; Rogoff’s conservative central banker) supports an aggressive, expectations-anchoring response at the zero lower bound/liquidity-trap margin to stabilize output without risking near-term inflation overshoot. Netting these insights, the tone remains negative but is tempered by policy actions that, in New Keynesian and credit-view frameworks, should cushion the downturn.
